title: Add command palette project creation workflow and extensible command providers
AI Elements chat UI refactor (issue 13)
description:
Background:
Refactor the chat session UI to fully adopt AI Elements chatbot components and AI SDK-style message parts. The current UI is a minimal custom implementation (Conversation/Message/PromptInput) with text-only streaming and a flat message schema.

Goals:
- Replace custom chat session UI with AI Elements chatbot components and conventions.
- Support structured message parts (text, attachments, reasoning, tools, sources, citations, etc.).
- Preserve existing projects/workspaces/sessions UX and routing.

Non-goals:
- Redesign of non-chat views unless integration requires it.
- Code/Voice/Workflow components not needed for chat.
- Backend changes unrelated to chat message parts and streaming.

References:
- AI Elements chatbot components: https://ai-sdk.dev/elements/components
- GitHub issue 13: https://github.com/ejohane/maestro/issues/13
acceptance_criteria: Chat session UI is fully AI Elements-based, supports structured message parts in API+UI, and remains consistent with existing app UX.
notes: This epic is the umbrella for phased delivery, dependency alignment, schema changes, UI integration, and QA. Child issues include detailed reasoning, risks, and acceptance criteria to preserve context for future work.

title: Phase 1: Foundation and dependency alignment
description:
Purpose:
Establish the dependency and component foundations required by AI Elements (React/Tailwind, shadcn/ui primitives, and Streamdown styles).

Rationale:
AI Elements assumes React 19 and Tailwind 4 for component primitives, utility classes, and streaming markdown styles. This phase makes the later UI work deterministic and avoids refactoring twice.
acceptance_criteria: Decision is made on React/Tailwind path; required dependencies and core styles are in place or explicitly backported.

title: Decision: React 19 + Tailwind 4 vs backport
description:
Scope:
Evaluate feasibility, risk, and cost of upgrading to React 19 + Tailwind 4 versus backporting AI Elements to React 18/TW3.

Considerations:
- Compatibility with existing dependencies and build tooling.
- Effort to resolve Tailwind v4 changes and potential CSS regressions.
- React 19 peer dependency alignment and library support.
- Timeline impact vs long-term maintenance cost.

Deliverable:
A documented decision with rationale, chosen path, and any required mitigation work.
acceptance_criteria: Decision is recorded in issue notes with the chosen path and rationale; follow-up tasks are linked/adjusted accordingly.
notes:
Decision: upgrade to React 19 + Tailwind 4 (no backport).

Rationale:
- AI Elements is built for React 19/TW4; backport would be higher effort and long-term maintenance burden.
- Only the web app uses React/Tailwind today, so the blast radius is limited.
- Current deps (Radix, TanStack, Vite) are expected to support React 19; Tailwind config is minimal with no custom plugins.
- Upfront migration cost is lower than ongoing divergence and CSS drift from a backport.

Follow-ups:
- Proceed with maestro-kn9.1.2 and maestro-kn9.1.3.
- Cancel maestro-kn9.1.4 (backport path).

title: Upgrade to React 19
description:
Scope:
Upgrade React and related packages (react, react-dom, types, testing utils) to React 19.

Key steps:
- Update package.json dependencies and lockfile.
- Resolve peer dependency conflicts.
- Validate rendering and concurrent features where relevant.

Risks:
- Incompatibilities with existing libraries or custom hooks.
acceptance_criteria: App compiles and runs on React 19 with no runtime errors in core flows.
notes: Only proceed if the decision gate selects the upgrade path. Close if backport is chosen.

title: Upgrade to Tailwind 4
description:
Scope:
Upgrade Tailwind to v4 and update build/postcss configuration and CSS inputs.

Key steps:
- Update tailwind/postcss config to v4 conventions.
- Verify generated utilities and update any breaking class usage.
- Rebuild and check for styling regressions in chat views.
acceptance_criteria: Tailwind 4 builds cleanly and existing UI renders without major regressions.
notes: Only proceed if the decision gate selects the upgrade path. Close if backport is chosen.

title: Backport AI Elements to React 18/Tailwind 3
description:
Scope:
Adapt AI Elements components to run on React 18 and Tailwind 3 without a full framework upgrade.

Key steps:
- Audit components for React 19-only patterns and adjust.
- Map Tailwind 4 utilities to Tailwind 3 equivalents.
- Add polyfills or local shims where needed.
acceptance_criteria: AI Elements chatbot components render and function on React 18/Tailwind 3 with acceptable fidelity.
notes: Closed: decision favors upgrading to React 19 + Tailwind 4 (see maestro-kn9.1.1). Backport path no longer needed.

title: Add missing shadcn/ui primitives and Radix deps
description:
Scope:
Install or vendor required UI primitives used by AI Elements (hover-card, scroll-area, select, command, popover, switch, dialog helpers, etc.).

Rationale:
AI Elements components assume these primitives exist; missing pieces block rendering and interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Required primitives are available in the codebase and can be imported by AI Elements components without placeholders.
notes: After decision gate, update dependencies to match the chosen React/Tailwind path.

title: Install AI Elements chatbot components
description:
Scope:
Install or vendor AI Elements chatbot components into apps/web/src/components/ai-elements and align imports.

Key steps:
- Add components per AI Elements docs (Conversation, Message suite, PromptInput, etc.).
- Ensure component exports are accessible to the chat view.
- Remove or quarantine legacy custom placeholders.
acceptance_criteria: AI Elements components are present and buildable in the repo with no missing imports.
notes: Depends on foundational dependencies and primitives.

title: Add Streamdown styles
description:
Scope:
Include Streamdown styles in apps/web/src/index.css per AI Elements guidance.

Rationale:
Streamdown powers markdown rendering for streaming AI responses and provides required base styles.
acceptance_criteria: Streamdown styles load with no build warnings; markdown rendering matches expected AI Elements look.

title: Phase 2: Message schema and API contract
description:
Purpose:
Define and implement structured message parts across streaming (SSE) and persisted transcripts.

Rationale:
AI Elements rendering relies on typed parts (text, reasoning, tool, sources, attachments). Without a shared contract, UI integration remains a fragile mapping layer.
acceptance_criteria: Server and client share a structured message schema; SSE and transcript storage deliver parts, not just text.

title: Define structured message schema and part mapping
description:
Scope:
Define a shared message schema aligned with AI SDK UIMessage parts (text, reasoning, tool, sources, files, data-*, etc.).

Key steps:
- Decide on canonical schema (adopt AI SDK UIMessage or local schema with mapping).
- Specify part payload shapes and metadata (tool approvals, citations, attachment refs).
- Document backward compatibility handling for legacy text-only messages.
acceptance_criteria: Schema is documented and referenced by server and client work; legacy mapping rules are clear.
notes: This is the contract gate for streaming and transcript changes.

title: Update SSE to stream structured parts
description:
Scope:
Modify chat stream endpoint to emit structured part updates (e.g., message.part.updated or equivalent), not only plain text.

Key steps:
- Extend event payloads to include part type and delta.
- Ensure message_end includes final parts metadata.
- Preserve compatibility for existing clients during transition.
acceptance_criteria: SSE emits structured part updates and the client can render them without lossy conversions.
notes: Depends on the schema definition; coordinate with client parsing.

title: Persist structured parts in transcript storage
description:
Scope:
Update transcript persistence to store message parts and metadata rather than flat role/content only.

Key steps:
- Define storage format and migration strategy.
- Add migrations or versioning if required.
- Ensure read path can return both new and legacy formats.
acceptance_criteria: Transcripts can be stored and retrieved with structured parts; legacy transcripts still load gracefully.
notes: Coordinate with schema definition and client parser.

title: Update client types and parser for structured parts
description:
Scope:
Update the frontend message model to match the new schema and provide parsing/mapping utilities.

Key steps:
- Replace ChatMessage with UIMessage-like model.
- Provide helpers to map SSE events to local state.
- Ensure legacy transcript conversion path exists.
acceptance_criteria: Client state uses structured message parts and renders without loss of data.

title: Legacy compatibility and migration strategy
description:
Scope:
Define how old text-only transcripts and streams remain functional or are migrated.

Key steps:
- Create mapping or migration plan (on read, on write, or batch).
- Document expected behavior for mixed-format sessions.
- Add telemetry/logging for migration issues.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy sessions load and stream without errors; migration approach is documented.

title: Phase 3: Message rendering and transcript UI
description:
Purpose:
Replace the chat rendering stack with AI Elements Message suite and related components, wired to structured message parts.

Rationale:
This is the user-visible core: messages, attachments, tools, reasoning, sources, and actions must render consistently with AI Elements behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Conversation and message rendering use AI Elements components; all major part types display correctly.

title: AI Elements Conversation container and auto-scroll
description:
Scope:
Replace custom conversation wrapper with AI Elements Conversation, including empty state, scroll-to-bottom controls, and auto-scroll behavior.

Rationale:
AI Elements Conversation handles streaming updates and scroll UX consistently.
acceptance_criteria: Conversation UI uses AI Elements component and behaves correctly during streaming and message history load.

title: Message layout + Streamdown markdown rendering
description:
Scope:
Adopt AI Elements Message layout and Streamdown markdown renderer for message content.

Key steps:
- Swap Message/MessageResponse components.
- Ensure role styling and avatar placement follow AI Elements patterns.
- Confirm markdown rendering with streaming updates.
acceptance_criteria: Messages render via AI Elements components with markdown behaving correctly in streaming scenarios.

title: Render attachments in messages
description:
Scope:
Implement MessageAttachments/Attachment rendering with thumbnails, hover previews, and removal affordances where applicable.

Rationale:
Attachments are a core part type and required by AI Elements spec.
acceptance_criteria: Attachment parts render with expected layouts and interaction states.

title: Render reasoning and chain-of-thought UI
description:
Scope:
Integrate Reasoning/ChainOfThought components for reasoning parts, including collapsible sections and status indicators.

Notes:
This may require redaction or configuration depending on product policy.
acceptance_criteria: Reasoning parts render and can be collapsed/expanded without layout issues.

title: Render tool invocations and confirmation workflow
description:
Scope:
Integrate Tool and Confirmation components for tool call parts and approval UI.

Key steps:
- Render tool input/output/state.
- Provide approval UI for gated tools if applicable.
acceptance_criteria: Tool parts render with correct state, and confirmation UI is usable when approvals are required.

title: Render sources and inline citations
description:
Scope:
Integrate Sources and InlineCitation components, including hover card carousel for citations.

Key steps:
- Wire citation references in markdown to InlineCitation.
- Show sources list with metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Sources and citations render with consistent styling and accessible hover behavior.

title: Message actions, branching, and checkpoints
description:
Scope:
Add MessageActions (copy/retry), optional branching UI, and checkpoint markers where supported.

Rationale:
These actions improve usability and align with AI Elements expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Message actions are available and stable; checkpoint markers render where data exists.

title: Phase 4: Prompt input and session controls
description:
Purpose:
Replace the custom PromptInput with AI Elements input, add model selection, suggestions, and usage/context affordances.

Rationale:
Input UX ties together attachments, commands, and model selection; aligning with AI Elements ensures parity and future extensibility.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt input supports attachments, action menu, and model selector; empty state includes suggestions where appropriate.

title: AI Elements PromptInput with attachments and action menu
description:
Scope:
Replace custom PromptInput with AI Elements PromptInput, enabling attachments, commands/action menu, and richer input behavior.

Key steps:
- Wire input to existing submit flow.
- Ensure attachment uploads integrate with API or stubbed storage.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt input supports attachments and action menu while preserving current send behavior.

title: ModelSelector dialog wired to session model
description:
Scope:
Add AI Elements ModelSelector (cmdk-based) and connect to session model state.

Key steps:
- Surface model list and selection UI.
- Update session model in store/API.
acceptance_criteria: Users can view and change the session model through the ModelSelector.

title: Suggestion chips and empty state UX
description:
Scope:
Add Suggestion row for empty conversation state and initial guidance prompts.

Rationale:
Provides better onboarding and aligns with AI Elements default UX.
acceptance_criteria: Empty conversation shows suggestions and does not regress mobile layout.

title: Context usage indicator
description:
Scope:
Add Context component to display token usage/cost with hover details.

Dependencies:
Requires usage data from API; if unavailable, use stubbed data with clear labels.
acceptance_criteria: Context indicator renders and updates when usage data is available.

title: Phase 5: Advanced components and polish
description:
Purpose:
Integrate advanced AI Elements components (plan/task/queue/checkpoint/shimmer/citations) and refine empty/loading states.

Rationale:
These components provide the richer workflow and explainability UI expected by AI Elements-based experiences.
acceptance_criteria: Advanced components render with real or stubbed data and behave correctly in streaming states.

title: Plan component integration
description:
Scope:
Integrate Plan component for structured plan parts, including streaming shimmer state.

Rationale:
Plans are common outputs for agent workflows and should be surfaced clearly.
acceptance_criteria: Plan parts render with collapsible UI and streaming shimmer when appropriate.

title: Task and Queue components
description:
Scope:
Integrate Task list and Queue components for structured task/queue parts.

Key steps:
- Render list items with status/progress.
- Ensure collapse/expand behaviors work in mobile.
acceptance_criteria: Task and Queue parts render and update without layout issues.

title: Shimmer loading states
description:
Scope:
Use Shimmer component for streaming/placeholder states across chat UI.

Rationale:
Improves perceived performance and aligns with AI Elements UX.
acceptance_criteria: Shimmer renders in key loading states without causing layout jank.

title: Checkpoint restore flow
description:
Scope:
Implement Checkpoint UI and restore interaction for historical markers.

Dependencies:
Requires backend support for checkpoint data and restore action.
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint markers render and invoke restore action when available.

title: QA, accessibility, and regression validation
description:
Scope:
Validate chat UI across desktop/mobile, light/dark themes, and key flows (streaming, attachments, tools, reasoning).

Key steps:
- Manual regression checklist for chat sessions.
- Accessibility review for interactive elements (hover cards, dialogs, keyboard nav).
- Verify no console errors during streaming.
acceptance_criteria: No critical regressions; accessibility issues are documented or resolved.
notes: Runs after major UI integration; should be updated as components land.

title: Documentation: schema and UI integration notes
description:
Scope:
Document message schema, part mapping, and component integration choices for future contributors.

Rationale:
This refactor changes the core chat architecture and needs durable context.
acceptance_criteria: Docs describe the schema, streaming events, and how to extend part rendering.

title: Phase 5: Advanced components + polish
description:
Implement advanced components and final polish: Plan, Task, Queue, Shimmer, InlineCitation, Checkpoint, and Reasoning/ChainOfThought integration. Provide demo data paths and consistent empty/loading states.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Plan, Task, Queue, Shimmer, InlineCitation, Checkpoint components implemented.
- Reasoning/ChainOfThought integration wired and displayed per spec.
- Each component has demo data path plus empty/loading states.
- UI is responsive and accessible.
- Demo data paths documented or discoverable in code.

title: Phase 2: Structured message model + API contract
description:
Define and implement the structured message parts model plus SSE/transcript contract. Replace ChatMessage with parts-based schema, define streaming event shapes, and plan transcript storage migration including tool approvals, sources, and attachments metadata.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Parts-based message schema replaces ChatMessage with fields/types documented.
- SSE streaming contract defines message-part events, ordering, IDs, and completion semantics.
- Transcript storage migration plan documented (schema changes, backfill, compatibility).
- Tool approvals, sources, and attachments metadata included in model and API contract.
- Backward-compatibility or versioning strategy stated.
